intro.text: A device of Roshar powered by Stormlight held in gemstones, such as the spanreeds that let people write to each other across great distances.
A device of Roshar that works by trapping a spren in a gemstone and stimulating it with metal, such as the spanreeds that let people write to each other across great distances.

description.text: Artifabrians, the makers of fabrials, are said to be only a few years from recreating Shardblades and Shardplate, but this has never come true. Their biggest step so far is Jah Keved's half-shards, shields that can withstand a Shardblade, perfected only in 1173.
Spanreeds, the most widespread fabrial, link two pens so that what one writes the other copies, letting people write to each other over long distances.
Most fabrials can be used by anyone who knows how, unlike Surgebinding; some, like heating fabrials, even work without anyone using them.

items.text: The ancient Radiants knew less about modern kinds of fabrial than scholars today, though the stories exaggerate their fabrials.

Fabrials have been known for centuries, but invention has sped up only recently: heating fabrials and spanreeds are just a few decades old. Most research happens in Alethkar and Jah Keved, with Navani Kholin as an important patron.

A modern fabrial is made by trapping the right kind of spren in a specially cut gemstone. The metal frame around the gem stimulates the spren: pressing metal against a flamespren in a ruby raises or lowers heat.
To trap a spren, artifabrians lure it to a gem with something it loves; the gem must hold some Stormlight, but not be full, and about seventy percent works best.
Once the spren is examining the gem, its Light is drained quickly using larger gems around it, and the spren is sucked inside. Which spren a gem can hold depends on its type and colour.
Fabrials seem to work from their user's frame of reference: a spanreed used on a ship at sea passes on the ship's motion too, unless the user thinks of both spanreeds as sharing the same frame.
A fabrial used in a room lined with aluminium can't be sensed from outside, and a spanreed inside such a room loses its link with its partner.
Raysium conducts Investiture, letting Light flow from one gem to another.

Khriss's Ars Arcanum sorts modern fabrials into three kinds. Altering fabrials change an attribute: augmenters increase it and diminishers decrease it; they work best on forces, emotions and sensations.

Pairing fabrials are made in pairs that move together across great distances: conjoiners move in parallel, while reversers move opposite, so lifting one lowers the other. Pairing fabrials were discovered only recently.
Warning fabrials, called alerters, detect things nearby and warn their user; some can sense approaching people while ignoring chosen ones. Their range depends on how much Stormlight is in the gem.
Ancient fabrials, including Surge fabrials, don't fit these kinds and are grouped separately.
Spren react to different metals in different ways, mostly in line with each metal's Allomantic power, and several fabrial gems can share one frame to do more complex things.
Zinc makes a captured spren manifest more strongly.
Brass makes the spren withdraw and its power dim.
Bronze makes the gem brighten to alert someone to something nearby.
Pewter makes the gem express its attribute forcefully; it's used for augmenters.
Tin diminishes nearby attributes; it's used for diminishers.
Iron makes the gem attract nearby substances.
Steel makes it push substances away, though artifabrians haven't yet worked out how to build repellers.
Some fabrials make heat, and painrials can dull pain: Navani shows an early painrial easing an ache in Adolin's hand.
Rosharan clocks are fabrials, in standing and hanging kinds, and many have bells that ring the hour.
Some fabrials partly drain the Stormlight from gems to dim their glow, just for looks.

Attractor fabrials draw in particular substances. Shallan sees one gathering smoke from a fire, and at the Battle of Narak Navani unveils one that draws water from the air into a globe around its garnet.
Clocks are expensive but becoming common, and Navani has managed to make one small enough to wear.
The lifts of Urithiru run on conjoined fabrials and gears, drawing Stormlight from gems set in their railings; a lever sets the direction.
Thaylen ships, including Rysn's Wandersail, carry fabrials that help steady them in a highstorm.
Moneychangers in Celebrant use devices that move Stormlight between gems.
Navani's vambrace for Dalinar holds a clock and a painrial; her own can switch the painrial to cause pain, for self-defence.
Rushu builds Rysn a chair that hovers, by pairing it with a heavy weight that's allowed to fall a little.

Soulcasters are fabrials of two rings and a bracelet, joined by chains holding three gems across the back of the hand. They're used by touching a gem with the hand pressed against what is to be changed. Most can make only one small change, but about one in ten can make any change.
In one of Dalinar's visions, the ancient Radiants use a fabrial of topaz and heliodor to heal injuries.
The Oathgates are fabrials that use the Surge of Transportation to move everything on their platform to a paired Oathgate in an instant.
Ancient Surge fabrials were made by persuading Radiant spren to manifest in the Physical Realm, and work differently: a Soulcaster needs to be asked for help.
